candidates.source_name: Portál o veřejných zakázkách – Individuální elektronické nástroje (certified e-tendering tool register)
candidates.why_relevant: Official MMR-maintained list of all certified individual electronic tools (elektronické nástroje) usable for e-tendering in CZ, with operator names and tool URLs. This is the master index that enumerates every commercial platform in this cell in one page — E-ZAK/X-EN (QCM), Tenderarena (Tendersystems), Josephine (NAR Marketing/Sentinet), PROEBIZ profily, zadavatel.cz/e-zakazky (OTIDEA), CENT (Osigeno), KDV, eCentre, FirstBuySale (ANETE), x:tendr (RTS), Eveza (NWT), Athena/nasprofil (GC Logix), eZakazky (YOUR SYSTEM), PARC (PXE), plus special-purpose tools.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML scrape of the tool table; use as seed list to enumerate platform domains, then crawl each platform's buyer-profile directory.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language search on certified electronic tools, then fetch
queries_used: E-ZAK profil zadavatele seznam elektronické nástroje zadávání veřejných zakázek

candidates.source_name: E-ZAK (QCM s.r.o.) – e-tendering platform, multi-tenant buyer profiles
candidates.why_relevant: One of the two dominant CZ e-tendering engines; deployed as per-buyer subdomains (e.g. mfcr.ezak.cz, ezak.cnb.cz) and a shared instance ezak.e-tenders.cz. Indexing the E-ZAK deployment pattern gives access to thousands of buyer profiles including financial-sector public bodies. QCM (with PVU + Gemin) claims ~42-43% of all registered CZ contracting authorities.

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate *.ezak.cz subdomains + known standalone instances; scrape contract_display / contract list pages per profile; watch RSS/atom where offered.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs search + snowball from certified-tool register

brief: CZ e-tendering is a concentrated commercial-platform market layered on top of the state NEN/VVZ backbone: QCM (Portál pro vhodné uveřejnění, E-ZAK, Gemin marketplace) is the largest host of buyer profiles, followed by Tendersystems' Tender arena, profilzadavatele.cz, OTIDEA's zadavatel.cz/e-zakazky, and the cross-border JOSEPHINE/PROEBIZ stack, with a long tail of ~15 further certified tools enumerated in MMR's official register at portal-vz.cz. Because publication duties push every public and sectoral buyer onto one of these tools, enumerating the platforms and then resolving buyer profiles on them indexes thousands of buyers at once — the Czech National Bank, for example, publishes via ezak.cnb.cz with parallel profiles on Gemin and PVU. Aggregated mirrors and alert layers (Datlab/TenderMan paid, Hlídač státu free with API, Opentender.eu open bulk data, plus subscription watchers TenderMonitor and dZakazky) collapse this fragmentation into queryable CPV-filterable feeds and are the most efficient collection entry points. The main blind spot is the private sector: no CZ commercial bank publicly names an e-sourcing platform or publishes RFPs, so bank-side demand signal must be sourced elsewhere; 'Bidmall' and 'Tender market' could not be confirmed as CZ platforms and are recorded as negative findings rather than invented.
